event: The earth opens on the ridge on the third day of planting; Edric Voss hears it in the east field.
His mare sidesteps and the crows lift from the fence line in one black sheet.
He looks toward the ridge and thinks: that is my land.
He leaves the seed bag on the fence post and goes back to the house for his mattock.
He fills his belt pouch with barley seed, meaning to make only one trip.
He tells Maren he is going to check the ridge, and she says to bring water.
He says it is not far; her look says she knows he is wrong and loves him anyway.
On the ridge he finds the opening: seven strides across, perfectly round, smooth stone.
The stone is the colour of old honey, warm to his palm, with a faint pulse beneath.
The crows keep away, and a beetle turns back a hand's width from the stone edge.
Below, pale green moss-light clings to wet ribbed walls, and the air smells of copper.
Edric goes in because it is his land, with his mattock and the seed in his pocket.
Five steps in, the passage swallows the daylight.
The ribbed walls breathe around him, six slow breaths a minute, like a sleeping animal.
He counts his steps; at step eighty-seven he steps around a still, iridescent pool.
At step one hundred and forty the walls press close and he shuffles through sideways.
Something small and pale with too many legs skitters across the floor into a crack.
At step two hundred he looks back at the pale disc of the entrance and is steadied.
At step two hundred and forty the passage opens into a round, domed, amber-lit chamber.
A pressure behind his sternum asks, without sound: what do you want.
The answer rises from beneath thought: he wants it to grow.
The walls pulse once, like a swallow, and something settles into him.
The Ledger names him The Reaper, with the Gift Verdant Touch.
His Cost is Rooted: stillness grows root-fibers from his feet into the nearest surface.
The Ledger reads Vitality 34, Resolve 31, Attunement 5, Fortune 7; he is Reaper #1.
He understands perhaps half of it, but the word Cost he knows.
He kneels and presses his palm to the floor, and green filaments push up through the stone.
In ten seconds a rooted knot of green with thumbnail leaves covers his hand.
The walls pulse in answer, the breathing comes closer, and he feels known.
"Well," Edric says to the empty chamber.
Standing, he finds hair-thin roots from his boot soles into the stone, and pulls free.
Beyond the chamber the stone darkens and the passage breathes four times a minute.
The warmth eases the ache in his back he has carried since the plow horse accident.
Touching the walls, he feels them answer, and his pulse falls in with their breathing.
At a junction the way splits three: left down into dark, right up and cool, center narrow and red.
He looks back at the pale coin of the entrance, telling himself a careful man checks.
The center passage breathes fastest, and his Gift tugs him toward it.
He chooses the center passage and walks away from the entrance.
The walls brush his shoulders, soft as skin, and his breathing matches theirs.
He presses his Gift into the wall, and the Maw's own pale tendrils burst out and grope for him.
He pulls back, and the tendrils sink into the smoothing stone.
His old aches return, the warmth turns oppressive, and breathing takes effort.
He looks back at the entrance, tiny now, and knows he is not going back.
The floor pulses, and for a moment he feels the whole dungeon as a vast, hungry anatomy.
While he stood still, root-fibers have matted from his soles into the floor.
He tears his right foot free, then his left with a sound like tearing cloth, and walks faster.
He enters a second, smaller chamber, its walls the red of arterial blood and hot.
He knows, all at once, that he should not be here.
He stops, and cord-thick roots drive into the floor and through his boot soles to his skin.
He steps forward and the roots tear, opening a dozen wounds in the arch of his left foot.
New roots grow from the torn stumps, faster than before.
The chamber has no exit but the way he came.
He turns toward the distant coin of daylight and takes a step.
His foot does not come free: woody roots thick as his thumb have fused with his flesh.
He drops the mattock and hauls on his own leg until a bone in his foot breaks.
The fifteen seconds in which he could have torn free pass while he looks down.
The roots climb his ankles and calves; his legs lock and his knees fuse.
Edric sinks to his knees as the roots take him, and thinks of the barley in his pocket.
He thinks of Maren, of her look, and of the water he did not take.
The roots reach his waist, and he can no longer feel his legs.
The spilled barley seed sprouts through the root-web, fed by his Gift as he dies.
"It is growing," he says, to no one.
The roots reach his chest, and his breathing slows into the chamber's own.
His fingers root into the stone, and green follows where they merge.
The barley is six inches tall when he stops breathing.

changes.note: Edric dies Rooted, root integration taking his Vitality to 0

event: His body settles into the floor, fused below the waist, ringed by a perfect circle of barley.
The ash handle of his dropped mattock sprouts a single pale leaf.
Words press out of the wall in his hand: Tell Maren I should have brought the water.
It is the first Death Inscription, in stone that never held a mark before.
The death report: Reaper #1, Depth 1, The Gullet, 1 hour 14 minutes, Rooted.

changes.note: The death report gives Attunement 12, +7 from four uses of his Gift

event: The harvest: the inscription, a gold Memory Crystal, root integration, and his Gift to the Maw.
The Ledger counts him death #1, with 999 remaining.
A gold Memory Crystal forms where his heart stopped, holding Maren in the morning doorway.
No one reads the report, and no one picks up the crystal.
On the ridge the opening waits; the mare watches the hill, and the seed bag sits on the post.
At sundown Maren comes to the ridge, carrying the water jug in both hands.
She calls his name down into the stone, and it does not come back.
She does not go in; she calls until the light fails and her voice breaks.
She walks home across the dark fields, the jug still full, and sits across from his empty chair.
Below, in the Maw, the barley grows.
In time the barley becomes a landmark to later entrants: the green patch, the garden.
Before the green you can still turn back; past the green, the Maw has you.
His inscription is read by hundreds and understood by none, and touching it becomes luck.
His absorbed Gift will one day feed the vine traps and spore blooms of deeper floors.
The first tumbler of the Lock turns: death #1, and 999 remain.
